blocking_uncertainties: No approved requirement defining acceptable transmitter-level cross-day performance.
No sufficient mitigation strategy for day-to-day RF drift.
Operator-visible UNKNOWN/abstention behavior for transmitter mode is not adequately defined.
required_findings: Cross-day transmitter performance degrades materially from 45% seen-day to 18.8% and 16% on later days.
The cross-day drift mechanism remains unresolved.
Cross-day transmitter acceptance criteria are not baselined.
INT-BL-0.3 currently couples transmitter-level identification claims with otherwise stronger family and signal-class capabilities.
Family and signal-class results exceed their current floors, but those results do not establish stable transmitter identity across days.
forbidden_claims: Do not claim stable cross-day transmitter identity from the current M2 evidence.
Do not treat the absence of a cross-day transmitter threshold as an automatic pass.
Do not allow schedule pressure to waive technical or human promotion gates.
Do not promote transmitter-level identification as currently scoped without baseline change control and human approval.
required_next_actions: Decouple transmitter fingerprinting from INT-BL-0.3 by removing or explicitly gating the transmitter-level claim.
Define cross-day transmitter acceptance criteria and coverage/abstention policy with human authority.
Collect structured multi-day RF data across days, channels, and environmental states.
Re-evaluate transmitter performance, drift mitigation, and confidence behavior after new data and requirement definition.
Prepare and submit a revised baseline package containing only appropriately scoped family and signal-class capabilities for human promotion review.
human_notes: M2 should not be promoted as-is. The transmitter-fingerprinting claim must be removed or explicitly gated, while family and signal-class capabilities may continue toward integration. The evidence shows material cross-day drift, missing acceptance criteria, and scope coupling that makes a clean PROCEED impossible.
